notes:
PASS on the fake backend only: the evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level, and no hardware, live ROS graph, rosbridge connection or simulator process was started. driver.lock.json keeps authored_by kind=model, model_id=deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run_id=ros-pilot-next2-002, and reviewed_by null; no human review, hardware run or simulator run is claimed. This is a configuration-only ROS 1 RosDriver over rosbridge (mode simulated, risk R0, device_kind world.sim) with no Python native class and no native.py. The scope is deliberately narrow: the input-free pause action sends the fixed request {paused: true, admin_hash: ""} to /mujoco_server/set_pause of type mujoco_ros_msgs/SetPause and requires the application field success=true; the get_sim_info action uses operation read on /mujoco_server/get_sim_info of type mujoco_ros_msgs/GetSimInfo and maps only state.paused. Both services are advertised relative to the private NodeHandle "~" (mujoco_ros/src/mujoco_env.cpp:200-201; mujoco_ros/src/ros_one/ros_api.cpp:55 and :72). The pinned launch file names the node mujoco_server without an ns attribute (mujoco_ros/launch/launch_server.launch:55), so the package chooses the absolute namespace /mujoco_server and records the upstream tokens as source_name; a deployment that runs or namespaces the node differently must expose the services at those endpoints or change the driver deliberately. source_ref cites the registration lines. type_ref cites the generated-service include lines (mujoco_ros/include/mujoco_ros/ros_one/ros_api.hpp:51 and :63) instead of the callback signatures because the callback forms mujoco_ros_msgs::SetPause::Request and mujoco_ros_msgs::GetSimInfo::Request carry a trailing ::Request that the G7 type-token check does not accept; the include is the exact declaration of the same service type. Pause is bound as the simulator stop and as an input-free safe_state=True action. SetPaused stores running_ = !paused (mujoco_ros/include/mujoco_ros/simulation_control_state.hpp:88-95), the physics loop takes SimPausedPhysics when the control snapshot is not running (mujoco_ros/src/physics.cpp:297-302), and GetSimInfo reports paused as !running (mujoco_ros/src/interface.cpp:1219). This disables continuous running, but pending or externally requested manual steps can still advance physics (mujoco_ros/src/physics.cpp:314-340). The fake omits that queue; the acknowledgement does not establish quiescent physics or a frozen clock. It is not a physical emergency stop, and the package makes no robot-velocity or hardware-safe-state claim. The empty admin_hash is only the fake/unauthenticated deployment assumption: TogglePaused refuses paused=true when VerifyAdminHash fails (mujoco_ros/src/interface.cpp:57-66), VerifyAdminHash checks only in eval_mode (mujoco_ros/src/mujoco_env.cpp:1211-1220), and no credential is retrieved. Application success=false and transport service failure are preserved as DriverFailed, and missing state.paused is MHS.CAPABILITY.OUTPUT_INVALID. The fake is a package-local ROS-free RecordingRosTransport with placeholder paused state and placeholder negative switches; it returns only state.paused, not the full real SimInfo response (model_path, model_valid, load_count, loading_state, paused, pending_sim_steps, rt_measured, rt_setting). It runs no MuJoCo engine, physics, ROS node or simulator. Fidelity is engine recording, level F0, determinism none, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0, reset none and no snapshot/restore; the gaps name absent native dynamics, ROS nodes, simulator execution and hardware validation. NOT COVERED: pause=false/resume, model reload, world step, gravity and parameter services, robot actuation, shutdown, the other set_pause and get_sim_info response fields, TF, rendering, sensors, controllers and every other mujoco_ros service, action or topic. No numeric action input exists, so no Limit is declared and site-limits.example.json is not needed; the only gate warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, which is expected because there is no actuating limit to probe. test_driver.py keeps check_driver and runs nine cases: the gate, paused observation, the fixed pause request, observability through get_sim_info, application rejection, ROS service failure on pause, missing state.paused, service failure on get_sim_info, and e-stop latching (the safe-state pause remains available while the ordinary observation is rejected). The clone was left unmodified (G1 passed); no network, pip install, upstream import or upstream execution was used.
